A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reprocessed flux for highly beamed emission from compact objects is only weakly dependent on the inclination of the beam axis to the disk.

, in the absence of relativistic beaming, the emission from the disk is highly suppressed when the beam is directed away from the disk, but for beams produced by relativistic objects the emission is not significantly affected by the inclination of the beam axis.

the reprocessing of radiation by accretion flows is a very complicated process, and that one should not make any general statements about the reprocessed spectrum without taking into account all of the relevant factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the emission from disks irradiated by highly beamed radiation can differ significantly from the standard picture.
the reprocessed flux from the disk is not strongly suppressed for highly beamed emission, and thus that the disk emission can be used to probe the beaming geometry of compact objects.
the emission from the accretion disk is not necessarily a good indicator of the orientation of the compact star, and that in many cases the emission from the disk will be highly beamed.
